answer_key.title: Covenant Remote WMI Wbemcomn DLL Hijacking
answer_key.description: This dataset represents adversaries abusing a DLL hijack vulnerability found in the execution of the WMI provider host (wmiprvse.exe) for lateral movement.

verdict.assessment: An operator deployed and executed the GruntHTTP C2 agent on WORKSTATION5, using it to execute remote WMI commands against WORKSTATION6 with code injection into notepad.exe for C2 communication, while simultaneously the domain controller machine account requested directory replication rights on the domain root object, indicating preparation for credential harvesting via DCSync.

findings.name: DCSync
findings.behavior: MORDORDC$ machine account requested DS-Replication-Get-Changes extended right on the domain root object, enabling DCSync credential harvesting.
findings.reasoning: The event shows MORDORDC$ (a machine account) being granted DS-Replication-Get-Changes extended right on the domain root object, which is the precise permission required to perform DCSync attacks. This is not merely requesting replication; it's the authorization of the specific capability needed to harvest credentials via the replication API, making T1003.006 the most direct match over the rogue DC alternative.

findings.name: Windows Management Instrumentation
findings.behavior: GruntHTTP.exe C2 agent on WORKSTATION5 spawned cmd.exe to execute WMIC commands targeting WORKSTATION6 for remote code execution.
findings.reasoning: The operator used WMIC to execute a remote command against WORKSTATION6 via the /node parameter, which is WMI's mechanism for remote code execution. This is direct abuse of WMI for lateral movement, not merely command shell execution or discovery.
